sanskrit: sa prācīṃ diśam anu vy acalat | taṃ bṛhac ca rathantaraṃ ca viśve ca devā ādityāś cānu vy acalan | bṛhataś ca vai sa rathantarasya ca viśveṣāṃ ca devānām ādityānāṃ ca priyaṃ dhāma bhavati ya evaṃ veda | bṛhate ca vai sa rathantarāya ca viśvebhyaś ca devebhya ādityebhyaś ca- -ā vṛścate ya evaṃ vidvāṃsaṃ vrātyam upavadati ||
english: He moved forth toward the eastern direction. The Bṛhat and Rathantara sāmans, the All-Gods, and the Ādityas moved after him. Whoever knows this becomes the beloved abode of the Bṛhat and the Rathantara, of the All-Gods and of the Ādityas. But whoever speaks ill of a Vrātya who knows this is cut off from the Bṛhat and the Rathantara, from the All-Gods and from the Ādityas.

sanskrit: tasya prācyāṃ diśi | śraddhā pūṃścalī mitro māgadho vijñānaṃ vāso 'har uṣṇīṣaṃ rātrī keśā haritau pravartau kalmalir maṇiḥ | bhūtaṃ ca bhavyaṃ ca pariṣkandau mano vipathaṃ mātariśvā pavamānaś ca vipathavāhau vātaḥ sārathī reṣmā pratodaḥ kīrtiś ca yaśaś ca puraḥsarāv ainaṃ kīrtir gacchaty ainaṃ yaśo gacchati ya evaṃ veda ||
english: In the eastern direction of his: Faith is his harlot, Mitra is his herald-bard, discernment is his garment, day is his turban, night is his hair, two bay horses are his wheelers, Kalmali is his jewel. The past and the future are his two outriders; mind is his off-road track; Mātariśvan and Pavamāna are the two that draw him off the road; Wind is his charioteer; the whip is his goad; Renown and Glory go before him — Glory comes to him, Fame comes to him, for whoever knows this.

sanskrit: sa dakṣiṇāṃ diśam anu vy acalat | taṃ yajñāyāyajñiyaṃ ca vāmadevyaṃ ca yajñaś ca paśavaś cānu vy acalan | yajñāyāyajñiyasya ca vai sa vāmadevyasya ca yajñasya ca paśunāṃ ca (…) | yajñāyāyajñiyāya ca vai sa vāmadevyāya ca yajñāya ca paśubhyaś ca (…) ||
english: He moved forth toward the southern direction. The Yajñāyajñiya and Vāmadevya sāmans, the sacrifice, and the cattle moved after him. Whoever knows this becomes the beloved abode of the Yajñāyajñiya and the Vāmadevya, of the sacrifice and of the cattle. But whoever speaks ill of a Vrātya who knows this is cut off from the Yajñāyajñiya and the Vāmadevya, from the sacrifice and from the cattle.

sanskrit: tasya dakṣiṇāyāṃ diśi | ūṣāḥ pūṃścalī mantro māgadho (…) | aho rātrī ca pariṣkandau (…) ||
english: In the southern direction of his: Dawn is his harlot, the sacred Mantra is his herald-bard, [and so on as above in the eastern direction]. Day and Night are his two outriders [and so on as above].

sanskrit: sa pratīcīṃ diśaṃ (anu vy acalat) | taṃ vairūpaṃ ca vairājaṃ ca varuṇaś ca rājā paścānu vy acalan | vairūpasya ca vai sa vairājasya ca varuṇasya ca rājño apāṃ ca (…) | vairūpāya ca vai sa vairājāya ca varuṇāya ca rājñedbhyaś ca (…) ||
english: He moved forth toward the western direction. The Vairūpa and Vairāja sāmans, King Varuṇa, and the waters moved after him. Whoever knows this becomes the beloved abode of the Vairūpa and the Vairāja, of King Varuṇa and of the waters. But whoever speaks ill of a Vrātya who knows this is cut off from the Vairūpa and the Vairāja, from King Varuṇa and from the waters.

sanskrit: tasya pratīcyāṃ diśi | irāḥ puṃścalī haso māgadho (…) | paurṇamāsī cāmāvāsyā ca pariṣkandau (…) ||
english: In the western direction of his: Irā (refreshment, drink) is his harlot, Laughter is his herald-bard, [and so on as above]. Full moon and new moon are his two outriders [and so on as above].

sanskrit: sa udīcīṃ diśam anu vy acalat | taṃ śyaitaṃ ca naudhasaṃ ca somaś ca rājā sapta ṛṣayaś cānu vy acalan | śyaitasya ca vai sa naudhasasya ca somasya ca rājñaḥ sapta ṛṣīnāṃ ca priyaṃ dhāma bhavati ya (evaṃ veda) | śyaitāya ca vai sa naudhāsāya ca somāya ca rājñaḥ sapta ṛṣibhyaś cā vṛścate ya evaṃ vidvāṃsaṃ vrātyam upavadati ||
english: He moved forth toward the northern direction. The Śyaita and Naudhasa sāmans, King Soma, and the Seven Seers moved after him. Whoever knows this becomes the beloved abode of the Śyaita and the Naudhasa, of King Soma and of the Seven Seers. But whoever speaks ill of a Vrātya who knows this is cut off from the Śyaita and the Naudhasa, from King Soma and from the Seven Seers.

sanskrit: tasyodīcyāṃ diśi | vidyut puṃścalī stanayitnur māgadho vijñānaṃ vāso 'har uṣṇīṣaṃ rātrī keśā haritau pravartau kalmalir maṇiḥ | śrutaṃ ca viśrutaṃ ca pariṣkandau mano vipathaṃ mātariśvā ca pavamānaś ca vipathavāhau vātaḥ sārathī reṣmā pratodaḥ kīrtiś ca yaśaś ca puraḥsarāv ainaṃ kīrtir gacchaty ainaṃ yaśo gacchati ya (evaṃ veda) ||
english: In the northern direction of his: Lightning is his harlot, Thunder is his herald-bard, discernment is his garment, day is his turban, night is his hair, two bay horses are his wheelers, Kalmali is his jewel. Sacred learning and far-famed wisdom are his two outriders; mind is his off-road track; Mātariśvan and Pavamāna are the two that draw him off the road; Wind is his charioteer; the whip is his goad; Renown and Glory go before him — Glory comes to him, Fame comes to him, for whoever knows this.

sanskrit: sa saṃvatsaram ūrdhvo 'tiṣṭhat taṃ devā abruvan vrātya kiṃ nu tiṣṭhasīti | so 'bravīd āsandīṃ me saṃ bharantv iti tasmā āsandīṃ sam abharan | tasyā vasantaś ca grīṣmaś ca pūrvau pādav āstāṃ varṣāś ca śarac cāparau | taṃ bṛhac ca rathantaraṃ cānūcye āstāṃ yajñāyajñiyaṃ ca vāmadevyaṃ ca tiraśce | ṛcaḥ prāñcas tantavo yajūṃṣi tīryañcaḥ | veda āstaro brahmopa barhaṇaṃ sāmāsīda udgītho 'paśrayantām asīdat | tasya saṃkalpāḥ prahāsyā āsan devajanāḥ pariṣkandā apsarasaḥ patnīr viśvāni bhūtāny upasadaḥ | ainaṃ viśvāni bhūtāni gacchanti priyo viśveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
english: He stood erect for a full year. The gods said to him: "O Vrātya, why do you stand?" He replied: "Let them bring me a seat (āsandī)." So they brought him a seat. Of that seat, Spring and Summer were the two front legs, the Rains and Autumn were the two back legs. The Bṛhat and Rathantara sāmans were the two lengthwise straps, the Yajñāyajñiya and Vāmadevya were the crosswise straps. The Ṛg-verses were the lengthwise threads, the Yajus-formulas the crosswise threads. The Veda was the cushion, the Brahman priest the headrest, the Sāman the seat-cover, the Udgītha the back support. His jest-companions were the devajanāḥ (divine folk), the apsarases were his consorts-in-waiting, all beings were his attendants. All beings come to him, and he becomes beloved of all beings — whoever knows this.

sanskrit: tasmai prācyā diśaḥ | vāsantau māsau goptārāv akurvan bṛhac ca rathantaraṃ cānuṣṭhātārau | vāsantāv enaṃ māsau prācyā diśo gopāyato bṛhac ca rathantaraṃ cānutiṣṭhato ya (evaṃ veda) ||
english: For him, from the eastern direction: they made the two spring months his guardians and the Bṛhat and Rathantara his attendants. The two spring months guard him from the eastern direction, and the Bṛhat and Rathantara wait upon him — for whoever knows this.

sanskrit: tasmai dakṣiṇāyā diśaḥ | graiṣmau māsau goptārāv akurvan yajñāyajñiyaṃ ca vāmadevyaṃ cānuṣṭhātārau | graiṣmāv enaṃ māsau dakṣiṇāyā diśo gopāyato yajñāyajñiyaṃ ca vāmadevyaṃ cā(nu …) ||
english: For him, from the southern direction: they made the two summer months his guardians and the Yajñāyajñiya and Vāmadevya his attendants. The two summer months guard him from the southern direction, and the Yajñāyajñiya and Vāmadevya wait upon him — for whoever knows this.

sanskrit: tasmai pratīcyā diśaḥ | vārṣikau māsau goptārāv akurvan vairūpaṃ ca vairājaṃ cānuṣṭhātārau | vārṣikāv enaṃ māsau pratīcyā diśo gopāyato vairūpaṃ ca vairājaṃ cā(nu …) ||
english: For him, from the western direction: they made the two rainy-season months his guardians and the Vairūpa and Vairāja his attendants. The two rainy-season months guard him from the western direction, and the Vairūpa and Vairāja wait upon him — for whoever knows this.

sanskrit: tasmā udīcyā diśaḥ | śaradau māsau goptārāv akurvañ chyaitaṃ ca naudhasaṃ cānuṣṭātārau | śāradāvenaṃ māsā udīcyā diśo gopāyataḥ śyaitaṃ ca naidhasaṃ cā(nu …) ||
english: For him, from the northern direction: they made the two autumnal months his guardians and the Śyaita and Naudhasa his attendants. The two autumnal months guard him from the northern direction, and the Śyaita and Naudhasa wait upon him — for whoever knows this.

sanskrit: tasmai dhruvāyā diśaḥ | haimanau māsau goptārāv akurvan bhūmiṃ cāgniṃ cānuṣṭhātārau | haimanāv enaṃ māsau dhruvāyā diśo gopāyato bhūmiś cāgniś ca(nu …) ||
english: For him, from the fixed (nadir) direction: they made the two winter months his guardians and Earth and Fire his attendants. The two winter months guard him from the fixed direction, and Earth and Fire wait upon him — for whoever knows this.

sanskrit: tasmā ūrdhvāyā diśaḥ | śaiśirau māsau goptārāv akurvan divaṃ cādityaṃ cānuṣṭhātārau | śaiśirāv enaṃ māsā ūrdhvāyā diśo gopāyato dyauś cādityaścānu tiṣṭhato ya evaṃ veda ||
english: For him, from the upward direction: they made the two cool-season months his guardians and Heaven and the Sun his attendants. The two cool-season months guard him from the upward direction, and Heaven and the Sun wait upon him — for whoever knows this.
